subject.title: feat: AI safety event taxonomy — plugin emission API and manifest policy

question: Should OpenClaw adopt this six-event taxonomy and manifest-authorized third-party emission mechanism as a permanent public plugin SDK contract?
rationale: The choice creates a lasting compatibility and security boundary for third-party plugins; source correctness alone cannot decide the event vocabulary, trust semantics, or whether external plugins should emit operator-facing safety findings.

options.title: Define the contract first
options.body: Keep the linked feature issue canonical, agree on taxonomy and host-owned authorization/session rules, then revise this PR to that contract.

options.title: Narrow to core-only events
options.body: Land only trusted core diagnostic contracts and defer third-party emission until a concrete external detector proves the API requirement.

options.title: Sponsor the proposed direction
options.body: Approve the six-event public contract, then require all correctness, compatibility, security, documentation, and real-proof blockers to be resolved before merge.

recommendation.title: Define the contract first
recommendation.body: Keep the linked feature issue canonical, agree on taxonomy and host-owned authorization/session rules, then revise this PR to that contract.

likelyOwner.reason: Their recent plugin manifest and SDK review history makes them the strongest available owner for the permanent public-contract decision.
